hero.title: VIGIL
hero.subtitle: VIGIL integrates satellite imagery, artificial intelligence, alongside field validation to early-detect and visually map deforestation risks, thereby empowering faster, more effective conservation actions in Vietnam as well as globally.

mapInfo.title: What is VIGIL Map?
mapInfo.desc: This interactive map visualizes the outputs of our machine learning pipeline across K'Bang and Mang Yang districts, Gia Lai Province, as translated from satellite data into actionable risk intelligence. Each 1 km² grid cell is assigned a deforestation risk probability generated by our Random Forest model, color-coded across three tiers: high risk (>0.7), medium risk (0.4–0.7), and low risk (<0.4). Warning zones highlight the top 10% highest-risk cells, providing forest rangers and conservation planners with a prioritized, data-driven foundation for patrol deployment. As a next step, we are expanding our dataset to scale this map to full national coverage across Vietnam in 2026. *Note: These outputs represent pilot model predictions and serve as prioritization zones — not legal proof of forest loss.

about.hero_title: Join VIGIL in protecting our forests!
about.brand_story_subtitle: From Field Expedition to Sustainable Impact
about.brand_story_p1: VIGIL was born from a field expedition conducted by its founding team at Cúc Phương National Park. Witnessing firsthand the decline of forest ecosystems, the loss of biodiversity, and the increasingly visible impacts of climate change inspired a fundamental question: How can technology play a more meaningful role in protecting nature?
about.brand_story_p2: Through these experiences, we came to recognize that forests are more than valuable ecosystems, they are natural defenses against floods, landslides, and other climate-related disasters. As forests continue to disappear, the risks faced by both people and the environment continue to grow.
about.brand_story_p3: This realization led to the creation of VIGIL, with a mission to harness artificial intelligence (AI) and satellite data to detect deforestation risks at an early stage, enabling conservation stakeholders to respond more effectively and in a timely manner. At VIGIL, we believe that AI is more than just a technology. When applied with purpose, scientific knowledge, and a commitment to environmental stewardship, it becomes a powerful tool for protecting forests and advancing a more sustainable future.
about.vision_desc: To become a leading AI-powered ecosystem for forest monitoring and early deforestation risk detection, uniting technology, communities, and public engagement to advance ecosystem conservation and sustainable development in Vietnam and beyond.
about.mission_desc: To build an intelligent forest conservation ecosystem by integrating satellite data, artificial intelligence (AI), scientific research, community participation, and public engagement to detect deforestation risks early, support informed decision-making, and drive effective conservation action.
about.trip_1_title: VIGIL's Journey Began in Ninh Bình (2025)
about.trip_1_desc: VIGIL's journey began during a volunteer expedition to Ninh Bình in 2025. By working alongside forest rangers and conservation practitioners, the founding team gained firsthand experience in forest restoration, wildlife rehabilitation, and field monitoring. These experiences provided a deeper understanding of the growing threats to forests and the challenges facing conservation efforts, inspiring the team to develop an AI-powered solution that supports more effective and sustainable forest protection.
about.trip_2_title: Deforestation Risk Map for Gia Lai
about.trip_2_desc: Leveraging long-term satellite observations and machine learning, VIGIL has developed a deforestation risk map for Gia Lai Province. By analyzing more than 6,000 1 km² grid cells, the platform identifies high-risk areas and provides early-warning insights that help forest rangers and conservation organizations make faster, data-driven decisions and intervene before forest loss escalates.
about.trip_3_desc: After completing the deforestation risk map, the VIGIL team conducted a three-day field expedition in Gia Lai Province to validate the model's predictions against on-the-ground conditions. Working closely with local forest rangers and authorities, the team surveyed high-risk areas, collected field data to improve the AI model, and participated in forest restoration activities. Through direct engagement with local communities, VIGIL gained a deeper understanding that effective forest conservation depends not only on technology, but also on sustainable livelihoods and nature-based tourism.

publication.hero_subtitle: VIGIL approaches forest protection through open, reproducible research — publishing findings that can be independently verified and operationally deployed.
publication.authors: Pham Duy Long · Nguyen Vu Huy · Nguyen Duc Anh · Do Nhat Quang · Dam Anh Thu · Tran Dang An
publication.paper_title: An Interpretable Machine Learning Pipeline for Deforestation Risk Prediction in Vietnam at 1 km Resolution
publication.abstract_p1: Deforestation monitoring requires reliable historical mapping and actionable risk signals that can be translated into operational priorities. This study presents a reproducible, grid-based machine-learning pipeline for deforestation-risk prediction and warning-zone generation in Gia Lai Province, Vietnam.
publication.abstract_p2: The workflow is developed in K'Bang District and evaluated for geographic transferability in Mang Yang District. Public datasets are harmonized at a 1 km × 1 km grid-cell resolution, including Hansen Global Forest Change forest-cover and loss layers, SRTM elevation and slope, CHIRPS rainfall, and Sentinel-2 optical bands and vegetation/disturbance indices for the 2023 reporting year.
publication.abstract_p3: On the provided train-test split, logistic regression achieved AUC = 0.931, AP = 0.926, F1 = 0.881, and Capture@10% = 0.190; random forest achieved AUC = 0.942, AP = 0.914, F1 = 0.878, and Capture@10% = 0.184.
publication.abstract_p4: For cross-district transfer from K'Bang to Mang Yang, logistic regression and random forest achieved AUC values of 0.743 and 0.767 and Capture@10% values of 0.170 and 0.145, respectively. This research has been accepted for publication in MDPI Remote Sensing (Q1, Scopus-indexed), with publication in 2026.
publication.methodology_p1: The study area is partitioned into 1 km × 1 km grid cells. Outcome labels are extracted from Hansen lossyear, harmonizing SRTM elevation, CHIRPS rainfall, and Sentinel-2 vegetation indices.
publication.datasets_p1: Public satellite datasets from Google Earth Engine including Hansen GFC v1.12, SRTM Digital Elevation Model, CHIRPS Climate Data, and Sentinel-2 imagery.
publication.results_p1: Random Forest achieved an AUC of 0.942 on the internal split and 0.767 on the cross-district transfer test from K'Bang to Mang Yang.
publication.future_p1: Scaling deforestation risk prediction to full national coverage across Vietnam in 2026.
